name: Aspartate Transaminase
overview: Aspartate Transaminase is a health topic that clinicians and patients frequently discuss during care planning in India and worldwide. Key considerations include aspartate transaminase (ast) or aspartate aminotransferase, also known as aspat/asat/aat or (serum) glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase, is a pyridoxal phosphate (plp)-dependent transaminase enzyme that was first described by arthur karmen and colleagues in 1954; ast catalyzes the reversible transfer of an α-amino group between aspartate and glutamate and, as such, is an important enzyme in amino acid metabolism; ast is found in the liver, heart, skeletal muscle, kidneys, brain, red blood cells and gall bladder. This summary is educational and should be paired with professional medical evaluation.
purpose: In routine practice, aspartate transaminase (AST) or aspartate aminotransferase, also known as AspAT/ASAT/AAT or (serum) glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase...
From a clinical perspective, aST catalyzes the reversible transfer of an α-amino group between aspartate and glutamate and, as such, is an important enzyme in amino acid metabolism.
Health professionals note that aST is found in the liver, heart, skeletal muscle, kidneys, brain, red blood cells and gall bladder.
From a clinical perspective, serum AST level, serum ALT level, and their ratio are commonly measured clinically as biomarkers for liver health.
In routine practice, the tests are part of blood panels.
